source.title: Benign Overfitting of Constant-Stepsize SGD for Linear Regression
source.authors: Difan Zou; Jingfeng Wu; V. Braverman; Quanquan Gu; S. Kakade

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. Its extracted front matter contains apparent JMLR template/placeholder details, while it also states that a short version was accepted at COLT 2021.
record.tranche_reason: The study sweeps training sample size and reports test-risk or excess-risk curves for synthetic linear-regression problems, a different model class and experimental setup from the original deep-network work. The text does not state the direction of those curves near an interpolation threshold.
record.gate_note: Figures 1 and 2 report risk against sample size; their plotted values are not recoverable from the supplied text, and the prose does not describe a rise in test risk as sample size increases. The paper does not sweep model size or training epochs. Cited results from other papers are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: This is a theory paper on excess-risk bounds for constant-stepsize SGD in overparameterized linear regression (benign overfitting). It does not set out to test any double-descent version. Nakkiran et al. (2019, 2020) appear only in a list of related linear-model work. Its experiments compare SGD with OLS and tuned ridge on sample-size sweeps. The prose never describes a peak, a rise in risk with more samples, or an interpolation threshold. Fig. 1 (d=2000, N≤200) never reaches N=d. Fig. 2 (d=200, N to 5000) crosses N=d, but no direction is reported. Nothing in the text bears on V1–V7, so the reader's 'tests/T2' should be dropped.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors give matching upper and lower excess-risk bounds for iterate-averaged SGD, set by an effective dimension k*. Benign overfitting occurs when the covariance spectrum decays neither too fast nor too slow. SGD is comparable to tuned ridge, can beat OLS, and tail averaging improves on iterate averaging. They draw no conclusion about double descent.
record.recipe_differences: Synthetic linear regression with constant-stepsize SGD and sample-size risk curves, rather than deep-network double-descent sweeps over size, epochs, and data.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors report that generalization depends on covariance spectrum; the Figure 2 experiment also varies the true parameter and estimator. The sample-size curve directions are not stated in the prose.
record.peer_reviewed: Annual Conference on Learning Theory (COLT 2021 short version accepted, as stated in the text)
record.problems: The sample-size trends are available only in figures in the supplied text, without recoverable values or textual descriptions of whether risk rises. The experiments report averages over 20 independent runs but no uncertainty estimates. They do not explicitly identify an interpolation threshold.

untested.parts: No deep networks; no model-size sweep.
No reported rise in risk with more samples near N=d.
No capacity sweep past interpolation in any model class.
The effective dimension k* enters the bounds, but no test of whether it predicts peak location.
Tuned ridge is compared with OLS, but the text says nothing about a peak or its disappearance.

missing.what: The OLS excess-risk curves in Fig. 2 (d=200, N from 0 to 5000) cross N=d. If read from the plots, they might show a sample-wise peak, and tuned ridge might remove it. The text does not describe either, so this is not usable as stated.
missing.versions: V3, V6 (only if plot values are recovered)

record.verdict_notes: Reclassify from tests/T2 to cites_only/T6. The paper is about benign overfitting of SGD and never claims or measures a double-descent peak. The Fig. 2 rows are method comparisons with tuned hyperparameters.

versions.untested_parts: Model-size sweep and a peak near the size that just fits the training set.
Test error over training epochs or other training-time sweep.
The sample-size sweeps do not explicitly locate an interpolation threshold or state whether more samples raise test risk near it.
Capacity sweeps across model classes showing descent beyond an interpolation point.
A test that one effective-complexity measure predicts peak location across axes.
Peak dependence on label noise or regularization, peak splitting, or disappearance under optimally tuned regularization.
A test of whether counting effective parameters turns second descent into an ordinary U-shaped curve.

rows.subject: linear regression problem instance
rows.operation_detail: Sweep sample size and plot train and test risk for constant-stepsize SGD with iterate averaging.
rows.note: The text says this setting generalizes poorly, but does not describe whether test risk rises as sample size increases; curves are averaged over 20 runs.
rows.check: Fig. 1 sweep has d=2000 and N≤200, so it never reaches an interpolation threshold. The text only says training risk is below Bayes risk and test generalization is poor. It cannot show V3's effect.
